title: Joel Greenblatt - The Investor Who Gave the Secret Away

reader_summary.source_label: From the episode notes — transcript not yet available
reader_summary.headline: Joel Greenblatt built wealth with patience and gave his secret method away for free.
reader_summary.overview: A young investor from Long Island entered the financial world without a fund or track record. He ignored Wall Street excitement and held six to eight stocks at a time. His patience paid off as he compounded money for a decade before sharing his method.

key_points.text: He built a portfolio of six to eight stocks at a time and ignored everything Wall Street found exciting.
key_points.evidence_quote: He built a portfolio of six to eight stocks at a time, ignored everything Wall Street found exciting

key_points.text: He compounded money at fifty percent a year for a decade before giving the whole method away for free.

reader_summary.why_it_matters: Patience paid off every time for this investor.

notes: In 1985, a 27-year-old from Long Island walked into the most powerful financial office in America with no track record, no fund, and seven million dollars worth of nerve. He built a portfolio of six to eight stocks at a time, ignored everything Wall Street found exciting, and compounded money at fifty percent a year for a decade. Then he gave the whole method away for free. Two years of his students quietly laughing at his old-fashioned criteria. Then the Nasdaq collapsed. He made one hundred and fourteen percent in a single year. Patience paid. Every time.🎧 Part of the Sleepy Stock Market series — financial history told as documentary audio.
